summary: Keep four borders — top, bottom, left, right — and walk around them: right along the top, down the right side, left along the bottom, up the left side, shrinking each border after use. Stop when the borders cross.

blocks.title: Read the matrix
blocks.text: `R C` on one line, the header `Enter the matrix:`, then R rows kept as strings (we only print them).

blocks.title: Four borders and the output list
blocks.text: The borders mark the rows and columns that have not been printed yet.

blocks.title: Loop while cells are left
blocks.text: When `top > bottom` or `left > right`, the remaining area is empty.

blocks.title: Right along the top row
blocks.text: Print the top row from left to right, then move `top` down — that row is done.

blocks.title: Down the right column
blocks.text: Print the right column from the new top to the bottom, then move `right` in.

blocks.title: Left along the bottom row (if a row is left)
blocks.text: The `if top <= bottom` check matters for a single row: without it the same row would be printed again backwards.

blocks.title: Up the left column (if a column is left)
blocks.text: Same idea for a single column: `if left <= right` stops us from walking back up a column we already printed.

blocks.title: Print the spiral
blocks.text: `print("Spiral order:", *out)` prints all values separated by single spaces.

complexity: Time O(R·C) — every cell is printed once; 100×100 → 10,000 cells.
pitfalls: Missing the `if` checks → single rows or columns get printed twice.
